sheets.title: One bar of chrome — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: The bottom nav was a full row of the frame, always drawn, for a choice made rarely: this is a vault, and a person lives in the vault. It is one key at the leading edge of the bar the phone already has. And `personal:/` was drawn twice in the same pane — the header opened with it and the status line closed with it. The one at the foot says more: it follows the cursor and carries the count and the filter, so the header keeps its command keys and drops the label.

sheets.title: The smallest phone — 320 × 568
sheets.caption: Chrome is the top bar and nothing else: 71px of 568. The list runs to the last pixel of the screen.

sheets.title: Where the sections went — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Five rows with room to be read, the open one marked, the wordmark at the head where a drawer carries a brand. Tab reaches the key, Enter opens it, focus lands inside, Escape closes it and hands the key back — gated. Nothing floats over the content.
sheets.before: five words dividing the width of a phone
sheets.after: five rows, each named at a readable size

sheets.title: Rotated — 844 × 390
sheets.caption: A phone on its side has 390px of height. One bar takes 55 of them, and the list has the rest.
sheets.before: a bottom bar eating the short axis

sheets.title: Desktop is untouched — 1280 × 800
sheets.caption: Captured with a mouse. The rail is still the navigation and the statusline is still seven keys; the only change is the list pane's header, which no longer repeats the tomb path its own status line already carries.
